newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Aussie under pressure as yen surges.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Aussie under pressure as yen surges.

text.p: *AUD to test downside again after failing atop 78 cents once more and with US$/yen on the skids through 117.00 yen support
*Heavy AUD/yen selling already taken it down two yen and more expected as unhedged Japanese investors cut long positions
*Many stops rumoured under $0.7750 and break risks $0.7690 *RBA governor Macfarlane speaking at 12.00 pm (0200 GMT)

By 8.00 am (2200 GMT) the local currency had indeed breached US$0.7750 support to be down at US$0.7738/43 from US$0.7782/87 late here Wednesday. Immediate support was now pegged at US$0.7735 with the recent US$0.7720 low the level to watch.
The loss of the latter would open the way to a long standing bear target at US$0.7680 and risk a full feldged retracement to US$0.7620 or even the mid-Feb trough of US$0.7550.

On the crosses the currency was down at 90.60/70 yen having dived as deep as 90.24 -- its lowest level since early January -- in scary early trade from 92.57/67 late here Wednesday. The drop brought its losses to almost 10 percent in two weeks.
The latest slip in US$/yen began after a surprisingly soft 0.6 percent fall in U.S. producer prices reinforced doubts the Federal Reserve would tighten next week.

This should have been positive for the local currency since a hike would narrow its interest differential over the US$, but the impact was more than overshadowed by rumours the Treasury had decided to call for a firmer yen.

There was no confirmation, but it meshed with recent talk in Japanese circles that MOF forex guru Sakakibara favoured 115.00 as the mid rate for US$/yen. Technical analysts said the break of key 117.50 support confirmed a trend reversal was underway.

On a chart view the dollar could be expected to fall to 109.25 in the medium term -- a 38.2 percent retracement of the rise from 79.80 to 127.46 -- while a full 50 percent pullback would see it to the 103.00 level Sakakibara recently mentioned.
The corresponding chart levels for AUD/yen -- its rally took it from 59.00 yen to 100.02 -- would be 84.35 yen and 79.50.

All this made domestic considerations look a little secondary but analysts were keen to see if RBA governor Ian Macfarlane would give a hint of the bank's view on the budget, and any implication it might have for monetary policy, at a speech around midday. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
